geometryPolicy: Authority-table points are used when surviving evidence does not support a defensible territorial boundary. These records must not be promoted to the possessions layer.

representations.label: Venetian Quarter, Constantinople
representations.rationale: The quarter changed jurisdiction and extent across three authority phases, while the available sources do not establish a parcel boundary precise enough for a polygon. The phased point records preserve those changes without implying cadastral certainty.
representations.chronologyNote: KAN-154 page verification: the 1082 Golden Bull granting commercial privileges in return for naval aid against the Normans is dated in Lane's Chronology and described at p68; the 1204 reaffirmation and extension over the whole Empire is at p68 with the partition at p43 and O'Connell p18; Michael Palaiologos retook the city in July 1261 (Lane p75); the quarter ends with the fall of the city in 1453 (Lane Chronology; p348). Day-level boundaries are editorial.

representations.label: Venetian fondaco at Tana
representations.rationale: Tana was a trading post under Golden Horde suzerainty, not a territorial possession. A port-authority point communicates presence and chronology without turning the fondaco into a sovereign enclave.
representations.chronologyNote: KAN-154 page verification: Lane dates the Venetian galley detachment to Tana to 1322 and the Black Sea build-up to the 1320s and 1330s (p129); a riot closed the port for some years after 1343 (p131). Neither anchor dates a fondaco beginning in 1332 or ending in 1475 — the window is retained as a documented editorial envelope.

representations.label: Venetian commercial presence at Trebizond
representations.rationale: The evidence supports a Venetian commercial presence inside the Empire of Trebizond but not a stable, surveyable quarter boundary. The foreign-port authority record is therefore the published representation.
representations.chronologyNote: KAN-154 page verification and documented discrepancy: Lane dates the large fortified Venetian quarter at Trebizond to after the 1319 commercial treaty with its emperor (p129) — not to the 1204 partition that this record's validFrom asserts. The 1204 start is retained only as the outer envelope of Venetian commercial presence; neither anchor dates the 1461 end at page level.
